title: Per-route shared-pool leakage after policy-schema migration causing silent under-enforcement
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
A migration of the policy schema (policy_v2 rollout) caused an interaction between the per-route quota enforcement and the shared-credit pool reconciliation. After migration we observed long-tailed cases where usage attributed to route aliases was not debited from the shared pool, allowing some tenants to temporarily exceed configured quotas without triggering throttles.

Observations: 
- Incident window: 2025-10-12 04:00–08:30 UTC (partial).
- Affected surface: per-route soft quotas and the shared org-level credit pool when route aliases and precedence rules were evaluated in the new schema path.
- Symptom: requests returned 200 while logs showed allowance > configured limit for ~2–15 minutes for affected tenants.
- Not a billing duplication: charges were attributed correctly later, but enforcement (throttle/429) did not occur during the leak.

Root-candidate hypothesis: 
During the migration we introduced an optimization that short-circuits evaluation when an alias-level policy matches and marks a route as "shadowed" for subsequent fanout checks. The reconciliation logic that drains the organization shared pool expected canonical-route ledger updates; shadowed routes used the alias key and the ledger lookup path skipped the shared-pool debit in the v2 code-path. The mismatch only appears when: alias precedence != canonical precedence AND a concurrent route-rename or policy hot-reload happened within the same reconciliation window.

Steps to reproduce (dev cluster):
1) Enable policy_v2 and alias-shortcircuit flag on staging.
2) Create org with shared pool and two route aliases A (canonical) and B (alias) with different precedence.
3) Send a burst that fans out across both routes while flipping the alias precedence (API call simulating route-rename).
4) Observe per-request decision logs and shared-pool ledger: some requests are accepted while ledger debit not recorded.

Logs / artifacts: 
- Sample trace IDs: trace-20251012-3a4f, trace-20251012-8bb1 (attached to ticket).
- Query: analytics.redis> HGET ledger:org-1729 route:alias-B -> returned null for debit entries during the window.
- PR with migration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/7421 (contains the alias short-circuit change).
- Design note: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RE/Policy+v2+alias+shortcircuit (design rationale).

Mitigations already applied: 
- Rollback flag: disabled alias-shortcircuit for runtime-1.24 canary at 2025-10-12 09:10 UTC.
- Emergency guard: added a temporary reconciliation run every 30s to detect orphaned allowance (>0 and ledger not debited) and to re-apply debits where safe. This reduced visible over-allow windows from minutes to <30s but is not a permanent fix.

Proposed fix (plan):
1) Update reconciliation to canonicalize route identity before any short-circuiting so ledger lookups are uniform across legacy and v2 paths. (owner: Arjun)
2) Add an invariant check in unit/integration tests: after any route-rename/hot-reload, the shared-pool ledger must reflect identical debit sequences for canonical and alias keys under concurrent fanout. (owner: QA)
3) Add a runtime assertion in dev and staging that raises a high-priority alert when debit missing_count > 5 in 1m for an org. (owner: infra-alerting)
4) Post-deploy runbook: schedule a reconciliation job and validate traces for a rolling 4-hour window after change. (owner: SRE)

Acceptance criteria:
- No unexplained acceptance of requests when org shared-pool balance is zero in staging for 24h under verified stress tests.
- Code merged with test coverage and runbook updated.
- Canary for 48h with monitoring showing no orphaned allowances.

Rollout plan: 
- Code change + tests -> internal code review -> stage canary (policy_v2 on 10% of traffic) for 48h -> expand if metrics stable -> full rollout.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- We can avoid canonicalization cost by doing on-demand canonical lookup only for reconciliation; this reduces reads at the expense of higher complexity.
- Temporary reconciliation increases DB pressure; need to verify redis latency under 1M keys.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Implement canonicalization approach and tests (Arjun) [ETA 5d].
- Add invariant checks to CI (QA) [ETA 3d].
- Update canary runbook and alert thresholds (SRE) [ETA 2d].
- Schedule post-deploy validation window and notify support/CS.
